Scope: phase 1 of the logistics area. Wet networks (sewerage, storm, potable water, fire fighting and TSE, including the force main), dry networks (medium voltage, low voltage, street lighting and telecom), the potable water pump station, the sewage lift station, guard rooms, all road layers up to the asphalt wearing course, and landscape.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 10-Nov-2026 data date the project is 65.1% complete against 83.5% planned, 18.3% behind the plan (SPI 0.78). It gained 3.0% this week against 3.4% planned, so the gap widened slightly from 18.0% to 18.3%.

With 85.4% of the contract time gone, 34.9% of the work remains. Finishing by the contract completion date of 29-Jan-2027 needs about 3.2% a week over the 11 whole weeks left, against 3.0% achieved this week, the highest of the last four weeks but still short of that rate. The weekly report's milestone sheet and the P6 update now forecast project handover on 22-Mar-2027, 52 days late, a week later again than last week's forecast. Construction is the weak phase: 55.2% done against 89.5% planned.

Weights are budgeted man-hours. This week storm water gained 7.7% and moved ahead of its plan, and sewerage gained 3.1%, all of it in testing and commissioning. No man-hours were earned on the potable water and fire-fighting networks, and the pump station gained less than 0.1%. The P6 update (data date 10-Nov-2026) has 4,851 activities: 2,831 completed, 580 in progress and 1,440 not started. Failed-start activities fell from 1,125 to 1,084.

The P6 update finishes the project on 22-Mar-2027, 52 days after the contract completion date. Most P6 milestones moved another 7 days later with the data date. Three networks now finish earlier: storm water on 17-Nov-2026 (previously 28-Nov-2026), LV on 14-Dec-2026 (previously 02-Jan-2027) and street lighting on 19-Dec-2026 (previously 13-Jan-2027). The schedule has no finish constraint at the contract date, so its float is measured against its own late finish. The asphalt wearing course has 5 days of float and construction finish 10 days. Other forecasts in this week's files: 07-Mar-2027 (General Information sheet), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's target date).

Share of each long-lead item delivered to site. Source: weekly procurement update 10-Nov-2026. By discipline (procurement summary in the weekly report), 114 of 160 materials are on site, unchanged from last week: civil and roads 61 of 82, electrical 22 of 30, mechanical 31 of 48.

Unit substations and RMUs reported deliveredThe procurement update now shows all 3 unit substations and all 5 RMUs as delivered, with an arrival date of 15-Nov-2026, five days after the data date. Every other delivered quantity is the same as on 03-Nov, and the weekly report's count of materials on site did not change.

Planned delivery completion: 27-Nov-2026 (electrical), 28-Nov-2026 (mechanical), 09-Dec-2026 (civil and roads). Materials approval: 147 of 160 approved, 3 pending.

Open issues and risks

From the progress presentation of 10-Nov-2026; the weekly report's Issues sheet and risk register are empty this week.

IssueOwnerDetail
Shortage of labour and equipment; subcontractor stopped workContractorPart of the project was assigned to another contractor and the company is providing its own labour; the presentation gives 543 workers, 306 items of equipment and 24 dewatering pumps on site. Labour and equipment must keep increasing to meet MODON's targets. Open since 01-Apr-2026 (223 days).
Culvert on the arterial road delayedContractorThe roof slabs of 32 joints are cast and their inner epoxy coating is done; the last joint is excavated. The work still waits for SEC to approve the proposal for protecting the existing cable. Open since 01-Jun-2026 (162 days).
Networks must be finished before road worksOtherThe subcontractor Unasco was removed and its approval withdrawn for not meeting MODON's targets. The contractor is working on the networks directly; its target to finish them by 19-Sep-2026 has passed. Open since 01-Jun-2026 (162 days).

A separate risk and issue log uploaded this week (status date 13-Oct-2026) lists the same three items, rated medium likelihood and medium impact, but marks the culvert risk as closed while the culvert issue is still open.

Data notes

  • Report week: the weekly report states "Current Contract Weeks: 67 of 78" (Milestones sheet). The report serial number (WPR049) and the consultant's inspection number (49) are not the week number.
  • This-week values compare this report with the 03-Nov-2026 report (previous week folder).
  • Four different completion forecasts: 07-Mar-2027 (General Information sheet, −37 days, the same as the Milestones sheet's "ready for initial handover"), 22-Mar-2027 (Milestones sheet and P6 update, −52 days), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's "target" date).
  • The P6 update has no finish constraint, so no activity shows negative float although it finishes after the contract date. 424 in-progress activities have finish dates before the data date (319 last week).
  • Monthly actuals in the Physical-Chart Data sheet change every week: last week they were raised, this week lowered again (May 27.9%, previously 29.6%; July 39.1%, previously 40.8%; September 48.7%, previously 50.3%; October 59.1%, previously 60.7%).
  • Physical progress is 65.13% in the weekly report and 65.27% in the progress presentation.
  • Quantities and man-hours disagree: Major Quantities adds 6,281 LM of TSE pipe this week, but the TSE network earned only 2.2% of its man-hours; potable water pipes (+263 LM) and fire-fighting pipes (+10 LM) rose with no man-hours earned on those networks.
  • The TSE pipe total is 57,419 LM in Major Quantities and 17,678 LM in the Conclusion sheet (79.3% finished there); the presentation's irrigation table raised its total this week from 17,678 m to 26,504 m with the executed length unchanged at 5,053 m.
  • Head count: for November the front page shows 360 planned and 484 actual labour; the Manpower sheet shows 78 and 538; the presentation gives 543 workers. Equipment is 329 in the Manpower sheet and 306 in the presentation.
  • Mobilisation: the weekly report gives 30-Aug-2025 as actual, the P6 milestone "Mobilization - Finish" gives 25-Nov-2025.
  • The "Complete earthworks" forecast moved back to 15-Sep-2026, a date that has passed, with earthworks at 96.2%. The "all materials delivered" forecast of 14-Nov-2026 conflicts with 46 of 160 materials not yet on site and delivery completion dates up to 09-Dec-2026.
  • Procurement: the unit substations and RMUs are marked "Delivered" with an arrival date of 15-Nov-2026, after the data date, and the weekly report's materials-on-site count did not change. The presentation lists 5 RMUs against 3 in Major Quantities, 377 street-light poles delivered against 380 on the lighting slide, 13 fire hydrants against 12, and 321 poles installed against 347 in Major Quantities. The workbook's procurement log is still unusable.
  • The weekly report's Issues sheet and risk register are empty this week. The separate risk and issue log is dated 13-Oct-2026, its dashboard shows #REF! throughout, and it uses project ID DAM2-01-029 and names the 3rd and 6th Industrial Cities.
  • NCRs: the front page shows 4 issued and 3 closed; the Quality-Stat sheet and the consultant's submittal log show 53 issued and 51 closed. Shop drawings: 1,774 of 1,774 approved in the weekly report, but 2,126 issued with 14 open in the consultant's log.
  • Sewer pipes are 89.9% finished in Major Quantities, 110.7% in the Conclusion sheet (6,805 of 6,146 LM) and 100% in the presentation (6,257 of 6,257 LM). Fire-fighting pipes are 101.1% in the Conclusion sheet.
  • Invoicing: the weekly report has 8 invoices (74.7M SAR) with none paid; the presentation still reports 62.9M SAR paid up to invoice 7. Contract value is 198,906,162.61 on the front page and 198,906,162.312 "incl. VAT" in the Conclusion sheet. The invoice log has stray values (21,100,000, 20,900,000, 200,000) and EAC shows #REF!.
  • Safety: the weekly hours worked have been exactly 34,740 in every report since 20-Oct-2026, and the November month-to-date equals that one week.
  • Key submittal dates are in Feb–Mar 2024, before the contract award of 30-Jun-2025. The look-ahead sheet still contains P6 data from the Hail Industrial City Phase II project.
  • The workbook's front page and the presentation also report cost-based progress; this report uses physical progress only.
